I also searched for downstream uses of the new definitions (orbitVisitSet, denseOrbitSetExp, escapingSetExp, EscapesToInfinity). The file has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set conflicts. The only concerns are missing canonical membership and unfolding lemmas for the new set-valued definitions. I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed simp lemmas would fire in the presence of existing mathlib lemmas such as Set.mem_iUnion and Set.mem_preimage. findings.excerpt:
def orbitVisitSet (U : Set ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  ⋃ n : ℕ, expIterate n ⁻¹' U
findings.problem: orbitVisitSet is a new opaque-ish definition with no membership characterisation registered for simp. Every use re-exposes the internal union-of-preimages form by hand, via `mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, by simpa [hzw] using hwU⟩`, `mem_iUnion.mp hzU`, and `mem_iInter` rewrites followed by `mem_iUnion`. The preimage membership step needs a separate simp call. Simp cannot normalise `z ∈ orbitVisitSet U` to the intended `∃ n, expIterate n z ∈ U`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_orbitVisitSet {U : Set ℂ} {z : ℂ} : z ∈ orbitVisitSet U ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, expIterate n z ∈ U := by simp [orbitVisitSet]` (or `Set.mem_iUnion`/`Set.mem_preimage`). Then replace the manual `mem_iUnion` / `simpa` steps in isOpen_dense_orbitVisitSet, mem_denseOrbitSetExp_iff_visit_countableBasis and dense_denseOrbitSet_exp_diff_countable with `simp`/`rw [mem_orbitVisitSet]`. The `⋃` unfolding should stay confined to this one lemma.
findings.benefit: The canonical form of `z ∈ orbitVisitSet U` is the existential over n, which is what every proof wants. This removes repeated hand unfolding and gives later users the same normal form.

findings.excerpt: def escapingSetExp : Set ℂ := {z | EscapesToInfinity z}
findings.problem: The set-valued definitions escapingSetExp and denseOrbitSetExp, and the predicate OnRealAxis (defined in Basic.lean as `z.im = 0`), have no simp-facing membership or unfolding lemmas. Proofs rely on definitional unfolding. For example, `dense_escapingSet_exp` ends with `exact escapesToInfinity_of_eventually_onRealAxis hm` and depends on `z ∈ escapingSetExp` unfolding by defeq. `escapesToInfinity_of_im_eq_zero hm` silently uses `OnRealAxis x` as `x.im = 0`. Elsewhere in the library, callers write `simp [ExponentialJuliaSetMisiurewicz.OnRealAxis]` or `simp [hn, OnRealAxis]` to unfold it. `simp` cannot turn `z ∈ escapingSetExp` into `EscapesToInfinity z`, nor `z ∈ denseOrbitSetExp` into `Dense (MulAction.orbit ..)`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_escapingSetExp {z : ℂ} : z ∈ escapingSetExp ↔ EscapesToInfinity z := Iff.rfl` and `@[simp] theorem mem_denseOrbitSetExp {z : ℂ} : z ∈ denseOrbitSetExp ↔ Dense (MulAction.orbit (IterateMulAct Complex.exp) z) := Iff.rfl`. Also add `theorem onRealAxis_iff {z : ℂ} : OnRealAxis z ↔ z.im = 0 := Iff.rfl`, ideally `@[simp]`, next to the OnRealAxis definition in Basic.lean. Then call sites can use `simp` instead of `simp [OnRealAxis]` and defeq-based `exact`s.
findings.benefit: Membership in these sets and OnRealAxis facts normalise to their intended predicate form without name-specific unfolding at each use. This makes `simp` and `simpa` calls such as those in Covering.lean and Results.lean robust and uniform.
